notes:
Summary: negotiating enterprise Dedicated capacity contract for Larchmont's global logistics routing and chat assistant workloads. Primary ask = hard throughput guarantees + strict latency SLOs for peak driving hours. Customer insists on reserved GPU planning (commit: 32x A100-similar) and a clear credit schedule for any SLA misses.

Recent activity / timeline (short bullets, CRM style):
- 2025-11-12: Initial intro call (AE Ethan Shaw + Head of ML Ops \"Marta Ruiz\"). customer profile: global fleet, precision routing, low tolerance for latency spikes.
- 2025-12-03: Architecture deep-dive with SE (Nadia Lopez). Discussed autoscale headroom, cold-start behavior, KV cache strategies.
- 2026-01-14: POC kickoff — 2-week trial on subset of routes (eu-west and us-east), baseline performance measured.
- 2026-01-28: POC result: 95th pctl latency ~160ms for 512-token context with batching; throughput sustained ~420 reqs/sec on 8-card pool. Notes: good but not at target for regional peak times.
- 2026-02-18: SLA negotiation call (fireflies ff_2026-02-18_7832). Customer requested 99.995% uptime, 5-minute P1 response, 1-hour P2. Redwood proposed 99.95% uptime, P1 15-minute incident response (acknowledge), P2 1 hour.
- 2026-03-05: Legal + procurement prep meeting. Draft SLA (v3) circulated; pricing deck updated to include reserved GPU amortization and overage tiers.

Key requirements (customer stated):
- Uptime target: wants 99.995% for core inference endpoints (routing + safety filter).
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 200ms for typical 128-512 token ops; p99 target < 400ms for critical flows.
- Throughput guarantees: baseline 5k requests/minute sustained during regional peaks; burst reserve 2x for 10-minute windows.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial reserve = 32 GPUs (A100 class equivalent), optional 16-GPU burst pool; preference for pinned model versions per pool.
- Maintenance windows: customer requests quarterly maintenance windows (2 hours) with 30-day advance notice; prefers scheduling outside pacific morning peak (10:00-14:00 UTC blocked).
- Credit schedule ask: tiered credit model tied to downtime minutes and % below SLA with cap at 100% of monthly fee; customer pushing for 150% cap.
- Support expectations: 24/7 escalation for P1 with phone bridge and named technical lead; SRE-level runbook access for on-call.
- Compliance: SOC2 type II, KMS integration for keys, audit log retention 7 years for certain segments, EU data residency for EU fleet.

Customer quotes / tone (paraphrased):
- \"We can tolerate occasional model drift but not outages during rush windows. If drivers get bad routes for 20 minutes, lost $xK/minute.\"
- \"We need deterministic billing for reserved capacity; surprise overages are a non-starter.\"

POC & technical notes:
- POC showed cache warm-up is the main limiter on p95 during sudden spikes; SE recommended proactive prefix caching and pre-warming job before peak windows.
- Suggested config: dedicated pool (32 GPUs), model pinned to rdx-llm-3b-q8 with fallback to rdx-llm-2b on capacity constraints; automatic routing policy with regional preference and cross-region fallback.
- Suggested batching policy: adaptive batching with 50ms max batching latency for chat flows, 10ms for routing microservice to meet p50 targets.

Commercial / SLA negotiation points unresolved:
- Uptime: REDWOOD draft v3 = 99.95% with pro-rata credits; Larchmont pushing 99.995% plus higher credit cap.
- Credit schedule: Redwood standard (sliding % by minutes under SLA, cap 100% monthly credits). Customer requested higher cap and faster payout cadence.
- Maintenance windows & notification lead time (customer wants 30 days); Redwood standard is 14 days for planned maintenance unless emergency.
- Support SLAs: clarify phone bridge and named SRE; trial period for rapid escalation to verify responsiveness.

Next steps (action items):
- AE/Ethan: collect internal finance approval timeline (due 2026-03-20).
- SE/Nadia: produce a refined capacity plan (32 GPU pinned layout + 16 GPU burst) with expected p95 numbers; deliver by 2026-03-12.
- Legal: circulate SLA v3 with alternative credit schedule options (99.95% vs 99.995%) for customer legal review; target counter-sign by 2026-04-02.
- Product: assess feasibility of 30-day maintenance lead time and escalate to infra owners if special handling required.

Stubs / references: pricing deck (drive link above), POC perf logs attached to support ticket INF-4821, engineering notes in INF-4903.
